newsitem.title: USA: Egghead Software to buy Surplus Shares.
newsitem.headline: Egghead Software to buy Surplus Shares.

text.p: Egghead Inc said it agreed to buy Surplus Software Inc for 5.6 million new Egghead common shares in a deal valued at $31.5 million.
The purchase price includes repayment of $5.6 million of Surplus Direct debt.
Surplus Direct had nine month sales through February 1997 of $35 million. Surplus Direct incurred a net loss for the nine-months ended February 28, 1997 of $1.2 million.
Egghead, with fiscal year 1997 revenues from existing operations of $259 million, is a reseller of personal computer hardware and software through its 86 retail stores.
The deal requires approval of both companies' shareholders at special meetings anticipated to occur in August.
The deal will be a tax free merger and will be accounted for as an asset purchase.

It will result in goodwill of about $24 million amortized over 20 years. The proforma balance sheet of the combined companies as of March 29, 1997 after giving effect to the acquisition would show shareholder equity of about $120 million and $75 million in cash. Egghead will provide Surplus Direct with a $2.0 million bridge loan that will be used mainly for working capital needs between now and the closing.
Surplus Direct shareholders will own about 24 percent of the outstanding shares of Egghead Inc if all of the employee stock options to be assumed by Egghead are exercised.
Orban also said the Egghead reorganization announced January 31, 1997 has proceeded according to plan.

Comparable store sales from continuing operations rose six percent in the fourth quarter ended March 29, 1997. The company cut its inventory from $92 million on December 28, 1996, the end of the third quarter, to $49 million as of March 29, 1997, the company's fiscal year end. Egghead's cash position at fiscal year end was $83 million, up from $70 million at the end of the third quarter.
